zuint columns from Arrow, through zuarrow

Source: R/arrow.R
zuint-arrow.Rd

zuint has no Arrow functions of its own. When the zuarrow package is installed, zuint registers its four types with zuarrow's registry as soon as both are loaded, and from then on zuarrow::arrow_to_r(), zuarrow::arrow_read() and zuarrow::arrow_array() read and write zuint columns exactly. zuarrow::arrow_registry() lists the entries:

Details

KeyArrow typezuint type
lint64int64
Luint64uint64
arrow.opaqueDuckDB's hugeint extension (w:16)int128
arrow.opaqueDuckDB's uhugeint extension (w:16)uint128
zuint.int128none: to = int128(), and writingint128
zuint.uint128none: to = uint128(), and writinguint128

An arrow.opaque column is DuckDB's when its JSON metadata says so at the top level: vendor_name "DuckDB" and type_name "hugeint" or "uhugeint". Other arrow.opaque types, which DuckDB uses for types Arrow has no form for, keep zuarrow's own conversion, as does metadata that is not valid JSON. The zuint.int128 and zuint.uint128 keys match no Arrow column: zuarrow finds a prototype's handler by its class, so each 128-bit class has a registration of its own.

A zuint prototype in to =, such as to = list(x = uint64()), gives that type for a column of any format, or a condition. zuint reads its own formats and the 8-, 16- and 32-bit integers exactly, and any other column through zuarrow's own conversion, then casts the values to the prototype's type. A value the type cannot hold, such as -1 under uint64(), 0.5 or the text "abc", follows the lossy policy below.

A decimal128(p, 0) column is a decimal, not an integer, so zuint does not register for it. Asking for int128 with to = int128() in zuarrow::arrow_to_r() reads one with p up to 38 as the 128 bits it holds, and to = uint128() reads its value, so a negative one is lost. DuckDB writes HUGEINT and UHUGEINT that way unless its arrow_lossless_conversion setting is on, and a UHUGEINT of 2^127 or more is then a negative decimal. So turn the setting on, and HUGEINT and UHUGEINT arrive as the extension:

DBI::dbExecute(con, "SET arrow_lossless_conversion = true")
zuarrow::arrow_to_r(DBI::dbGetQueryArrow(con, sql))

A null reads as NA and an NA writes as a null. A valid value equal to a type's NA bit pattern, such as UINT64_MAX in a UBIGINT column, cannot be held, nor can a value out of a prototype's range. zuarrow's lossy policy decides what happens to them, in zuarrow's condition classes:

  • "error" and "character" raise zuarrow_lossy_error, naming the column, its format and a value. "character" would give the column as text only for the batches that lose a value, which could not be combined with the others, so it fails like "error" instead.

  • "warn" reads them as NA with one zuarrow_lossy_warning per batch.

  • "allow" reads them as NA silently.

Writing never loses a value: int128 and uint128 are written as the DuckDB extension, which DuckDB reads back as HUGEINT and UHUGEINT.

See also

zu_storage() for the representation, the contract a package that builds zuint vectors in C relies on.
